name: Ideal Course Lab Template
description: A reusable Secure Stack lab template that emphasizes learning by doing, deliberate observation, and end-of-lab reflection.
learning_objectives: Explain what the learner is supposed to understand by the end of the lab.
Connect each practical step to a meaningful security observation.
Help the learner move from raw tool output to evidence-backed understanding.
pre_lab_context: Use this section to explain why the lab matters before the learner starts. Frame it like a class assignment, not a checklist.
environment_overview: Describe the attacker tools, the target system, and any browser handoff or forwarded service behavior the learner should understand before beginning.
reflection_prompt: What observation changed your understanding of the target the most, and why?
lab_takeaways: Summarize the first major lesson the learner should leave with.
Summarize how the lab connected a command or observation to a concept.
Summarize what the learner should now understand that they did not understand at the start.
prerequisites: List the background knowledge needed to succeed.
success_criteria: State what successful completion looks like from the learner's perspective.
Keep success criteria focused on evidence and understanding, not just clicking through the lab.

topology.summary: Explain the learning-relevant relationship between the attacker and the target.

nodes.label: Attacker shell
nodes.details: Describe what the learner can do from the attacker side.

nodes.label: Target service
nodes.details: Describe the exposed system or service the learner is investigating.

connections.label: Describe the recon or interaction path.

tasks.title: Step 1 title
tasks.objective: State what the learner must prove or understand in this step.
tasks.instruction: Give the learner one clear action to perform.
tasks.explanation: Explain why this step exists and how it sets up the next move.
what_to_observe: List the specific output, header, port, behavior, or visual cue the learner should notice.
Keep observation prompts concrete and tied to evidence.
tasks.why_observation_matters: Explain how the observation changes the learner's understanding of the target or environment.
tasks.learning_takeaway: Summarize what this completed step proved in one concise sentence.
tasks.expected_outcome: Describe what a successful outcome should look like.
hints: Use hints to keep the learner moving without giving away everything immediately.
success_criteria: State how the learner knows the step is complete.
tasks.remediation_text: Explain how to recover if the learner does not see the expected signal.

tasks.title: Observation or browser confirmation step
tasks.objective: Use this for browser-visible validation when it strengthens the lesson.
tasks.instruction: Open the forwarded browser URL and confirm the expected behavior.
tasks.explanation: Explain why the learner is moving from the terminal into the browser.
what_to_observe: Describe what should be visible in the browser.
tasks.why_observation_matters: Explain why the browser-visible result matters in addition to the terminal evidence.
tasks.learning_takeaway: Summarize what the browser confirmation added to the lab understanding.
hints: Use the launcher-provided URL instead of guessing the host port.
success_criteria: State the browser-visible condition that confirms success.
tasks.remediation_text: Explain what to verify if the browser step does not work.
